clue.text: Common to find extra starting price studied

parts.note: in cricket a wide is an extra, a run conceded for a ball bowled out of reach
SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price
to have read a subject is to have studied it

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a horse's starting price, once studied, turns out to be commonplace.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide is a cricket extra; SP is the starting price quoted on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something common is found in many places, so it is prevalent far and wide.

clue.text: You know if you've got it

definitions.text: You know if you've got it

parts.words: You know if you've got it
parts.note: the quality of sound knowledge and judgement: whoever has it knows things, though the surface suggests being aware of possessing something

explanation.surface: A teasing remark that you would be aware of owning something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'You know' literally: having this quality is what makes a person knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is accumulated knowledge and good judgement, the thing that makes a person knowing.

clue.text: Flirt with depression in Yorkshire? Book twice for lodging

indicators.note: lodging means housing something, so the doubled letter is put up inside the valley

parts.note: a dale is a valley, as in the Yorkshire Dales

indicators.note: the single letter for book is written two times over

explanation.surface: Someone toys with a Yorkshire holiday, booking a valley lodging twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are a national park of valleys in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To flirt with an idea or pastime is to try it casually and superficially, without commitment.

clue.text: Posed with one's works, revealed as adequate

parts.note: a model sat for an artist, that is, posed
one's can mean 'one is', and I is one, so I'S gives IS
a works is a factory

explanation.surface: An artist sat for a portrait alongside their works, which proved merely adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is read as I'S, with I as the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfactory is good enough to meet requirements, which is what adequate means.

clue.text: Estimate speed toll

definitions.meaning: the pace at which something happens
a charge or fee levied, as in a tariff

explanation.surface: A driver weighs up how fast to go against the road charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for assessing and as a noun for both pace and a set charge.

clue.text: They could be redirected to a star/sun?

indicators.note: redirecting points things a new way, so these letters are sent into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A question whether some travellers might be steered towards a star or the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a description: space travellers are the ones who could be sent towards a star.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the space travellers the clue describes, people who could fly to a star.

clue.text: Scoffs as regatta's jettisoning odd entries

indicators.note: throwing out the odd-numbered letters of the word leaves only the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a boat race that throws out unusual competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffs' looks like mockery but means eats greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is British slang for wolfing it down, consuming it greedily.

clue.text: Fit it up in renovated chalet

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the rebuilt letters
a renovated building is remade, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Instructions to install something in a chalet being done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT into TI, which goes 'in' ATHLEC, the letters of CHALET 'renovated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fit means in good physical shape, strong and sporty.

clue.text: Quiet before and after riot — disorderly but not very long

indicators.note: the call for quiet stands on both sides of the rearranged letters

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet, used here twice, once before and once after

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Calm both precedes and follows a brief riot.
explanation.walkthrough: The single call for quiet is used twice, standing on each side of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens an adjective, so this means somewhat brief, not very long.

clue.text: Reserve suite but confused about street briefly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the abbreviation
confused letters are mixed up, so these are rearranged

parts.note: ST is the short form of street

explanation.surface: Someone books a hotel suite but gets muddled over the street address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a verb about booking; it is the sports noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve in sport is a replacement player who comes on in place of another.

clue.text: Film finishes early — drive away

indicators.note: the word stops before its final letter, which is dropped

parts.note: to film a scene is to shoot it

explanation.surface: A cinema showing ends ahead of time, and the audience heads off.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection or verb means to send off or chase away, as with an unwanted animal.

clue.text: Release article on part of speech — stick with it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a noun is one of the parts of speech
cement is something to stick things together with

explanation.surface: Advice on a grammar point: put out an article, then persevere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick with it' sounds like encouragement; it names a binding material.
explanation.definitionFit: A press release is a public statement, a formal declaration put out for publication.

clue.text: Love and desire gripping student — would that be wise?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: gripping means holding on to, so the learner is held inside

parts.note: a desire is a wish
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A wry question whether romance and longing that captivate a student are wise.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is a traditional emblem of wisdom, so being like an owl suggests solemn sagacity.

clue.text: Second person with no starter to eat? Most immature

parts.note: the second-person pronoun is you

indicators.note: no starter means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to ingest is to eat

explanation.surface: At a meal, a second diner has no first course to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course of a meal; it means the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of young describes the least grown-up, the one with the fewest years.

clue.text: I invested in mobile top-up loan for residents

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the rearranged ones
mobile means able to move, so these letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into a mobile phone top-up loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone; it signals rearranging TOPUPLOAN, with I 'invested in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The people living in a place, taken together, are its inhabitants.

clue.text: Two groups of politicians to accommodate or a lot of researchers here

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the two parties take the other words inside

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour and Tories are Conservatives, two British parties

explanation.surface: Two political parties are asked to make room for a great many scientists.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour (LAB) and Tories are Britain's two main parties; OR A sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratories are workplaces where scientific researchers carry out experiments.

clue.text: Southern elite journalist was crying?

parts.note: the cream is the elite, the best of a group
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A posh southern reporter asks whether they were in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'crying' means crying out, not weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying out loudly is shrieking, so the past tense gives a loud shriek or yell.

clue.text: Case of Clarins tan certain to cover it

indicators.note: the phrase covers the letters, holding them within its words

explanation.surface: A tub of Clarins tanning cream that will surely cover the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Clarins is a French cosmetics brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is an example or occurrence, as in 'for instance'.

clue.text: Building engineer scorning TUC needing time to break

indicators.note: breaking into means entering, so the letter goes inside the rearranged ones
to engineer is to contrive or rework, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer who scorns the TUC needs time to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the federation of British trade unions. 'engineer' looks like a person; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Building means putting something together, erecting it from parts.

clue.text: Work over short speech of gratitude before getting to food

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
ta is a brief British way of saying thanks

explanation.surface: Someone goes over a short thank-you speech before getting to the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns OP (opus, a work) into PO. 'Ta' is British informal for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A spud is a staple starchy vegetable, an everyday item of food.

clue.text: Notebooks unopened? They're probably out swimming and running around

definitions.text: They're probably out swimming and running around

indicators.note: unopened means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: jotters are notebooks

explanation.surface: Unopened notebooks lie about while their owners are out swimming and running.
explanation.walkthrough: Jotter is the British word for a notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: These river mammals spend much of their time swimming and scampering along banks.

clue.text: Going on and on, getting cross inside and outside

indicators.note: inside means the letter is placed within the longer word

parts.note: something eternal goes on and on for ever
a cross is written as X

explanation.surface: Someone growing angrier inside and out after endless delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry'; it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the outside of an object is exterior to it.

clue.text: Investigation of lariat rope-running heading to the West

indicators.note: travelling west on the page means running right to left, backwards
of means taken from within, so the letters are drawn out of the phrase

explanation.surface: A cowboy's lasso, rope running out, heading for the Wild West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' takes TROPER from 'lariat rope-running'; 'heading to the West' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An official account of findings, such as a committee's, presents an inquiry's results.

clue.text: Incisiveness, let's say, of French revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: EG is short for 'for example', that is, let's say
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A sharp remark, perhaps, about a French revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a rebel; here it means turning round the abbreviation and the French word together.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge in someone's voice or wit is a sharpness, a cutting quality.

clue.text: This person's popular, being embraced by yours truly

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so this goes inside the other word

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being liked and hugged by the letter-writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to me, the speaker, this person.

clue.text: The fairy-tale king Hans had one, being Christian

definitions.text: The fairy-tale king Hans had one, being Christian

parts.words: The fairy-tale king Hans had one, being Christian
parts.note: Hans Christian Andersen, master of fairy tales, had Christian between first name and surname; the surface suggests faith

explanation.surface: A storybook monarch called Hans was a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' seems to describe his faith, but it is part of the writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian sits between Hans and Andersen in the storyteller's full name.

clue.text: Title that reads the same backwards

definitions.note: a title ... is the legal document proving ownership, so a title is this document

indicators.note: says the word is a palindrome, identical whichever way it is read

parts.note: a title ... is the legal document proving ownership, so a title is this document

explanation.surface: A name or heading that is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a title to property is proved by the document that conveys ownership.

clue.text: Objects, seeing lies getting Victor kicked out for tango

indicators.note: one letter is ejected and replaced by another

parts.note: inventions are made-up stories, lies
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
tango is T in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone objects on discovering lies that got a man called Victor dismissed for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' looks like a verb of protest; it is a plural noun for aims.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects in the sense of aims or purposes are what a person means to achieve.
